Getting started

Open the calculator by going to simeonlaw.info/calculator in your web browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari). No install, no login.

Before you calculate, set the basics at the top of the form:

  • Conference — choose NY or NE. This selects the correct rates and rules; the rest of the form stays the same.
  • Pastor Information — the pastor's name (optional, used only as a label), Clergy / Laity Status (e.g. Full Elder), Years of Service, and Appointment Time (Full-time, ¾, ½, or ¼).
  • These inputs determine the minimum salary and which benefit plans apply.

The two workflows

At the very top, “What do you want to calculate?” offers two modes. Everything else on the form is shared — only this choice, and the salary/budget box, change.

ModeYou enter…You get…
Total cost from a salarya salarythe full cost to the church/charge
Max salary from a budgeta budgetthe largest salary that fits the budget

Total cost from a salary (NY) → NE version

Enter a salary and the calculator shows the full cost to the church once benefits are added. This section follows one pastor — Rev. Morgan Lee (Full Elder, 5 years, full-time, parsonage) at a $60,000 salary — first at a single church, then across a multi-point charge, and finally exporting the result.

3.1 — Single-point charge

Use case: “We plan to pay Rev. Morgan Lee a $60,000 salary at one church. What will the appointment actually cost us once benefits are added?”
  1. Make sure the mode is set to Total cost from a salary (the default).
  2. Choose the Clergy / Laity Status (here, Full Elder (FE)).
  3. Enter the Years of Service (here, 5). The inputted salary is checked against the minimum salary for the selected status and years of service.
  4. Choose the Appointment Time (here, Full-time (100%)).
  5. Enter the Cash Salary amount (here, $60,000). If you enter less than the conference minimum for that status/years/appointment, a red note appears — that's a heads-up, not a block.
  6. Set the Accountable Reimbursement (ARP) — leave at Conference minimum unless you have a custom figure.
  7. Choose the Housing type — Parsonage or Housing Allowance.

Click Calculate.

1 The results table lists every component and the bottom line:

Line itemAmount
Salary$60,000
ARP$6,400
HealthFlex$22,200
Compass$8,910
CPP$2,430
Total Cost to Charge$99,940

So a $60,000 salary really costs the church about $99,940 once benefits are included.

3.2 — Multipoint charge

Use case: “The same pastor actually serves a three-point charge — Alpha, Beta, and Gamma UMC — who split costs 50% / 30% / 20%. What does each church owe?”
  1. Set Number of Churches to 2 or more (here, 3). Per-church fields appear.
  2. Choose how to divide the cost with the Even split / Custom split toggle. Even split divides equally; Custom split lets you set each church's percentage.
  3. Decide how to handle the MCAA multi-point supplement (explained just below).
  4. Fill in each church name and its Share %. The Total must equal 100% before you can calculate (here 50 + 30 + 20 = 100%).
About the MCAA. Serving more than one church earns the pastor the Multiple Charge/Appointment Adjustment (MCAA) — a NY supplement of $1,500 for two churches or $3,000 for three or more (there is no NE equivalent). You choose how it is paid:
  • Add to ARP (the default) — the supplement is folded into the pastor's Accountable Reimbursement (ARP) line, with no separate paperwork. In this example the ARP line reads $9,400 ($6,400 minimum + $3,000 MCAA).
  • Taxable stipend — the supplement is paid to the pastor as a separate taxable cash stipend (its own line on the result, no receipts required), and the ARP line stays at its $6,400 base.

Finish the rest of the form as usual and click Calculate.

1 The results table adds a column per church, and each column header shows that church's share — Alpha UMC (50%), Beta UMC (30%), Gamma UMC (20%). Every line item is split accordingly, and the amounts reconcile to the penny both across each row and down each church's column:

Line itemEntire ChargeAlpha (50%)Beta (30%)Gamma (20%)
Total$102,940$51,470$30,882$20,588

The $60,000 salary is the same, but the charge total is $102,940 — $3,000 more than the single church above — because a multi-point charge in NY adds the MCAA supplement (it appears on the ARP line, which rises from $6,400 to $9,400). Each church now knows exactly what to budget.

3.3 — Export a Statement of Understanding (.docx)

Once you have a result, you can save or share it — here, the multi-point charge from 3.2.

  1. Copy Table — copies the results table to your clipboard, ready to paste into an email or a Word document (formatting preserved).
  2. Export to SOU (.docx) — downloads a filled-in Statement of Understanding Word document with the figures already in place, ready to review and sign.

Total cost from a salary (NE) → NY version

This walks through the total-cost workflow in the NE conference. The NE-specific input to note is ACH billing for HealthFlex. Same pastor — Rev. Morgan Lee (Full Elder, 5 years, full-time, parsonage) at a $60,000 salary.

4.1 — Single-point charge

Use case: “The same $60,000 appointment at one church, but in the NE conference. What does it cost?”
  1. Set the Conference to NE. This reveals the NE-specific options and switches to NE rates.
  2. HealthFlex Billing — indicate whether the church pays the HealthFlex premium by ACH (bank draft). Leave it checked (the default) for the discounted ACH rate; uncheck it for the blended rate.
  3. Choose the Clergy / Laity Status (here, Full Elder (FE)).
  4. Enter the Years of Service (here, 5). The inputted salary is checked against the minimum salary for the selected status and years of service.
  5. Choose the Appointment Time (here, Full-time (100%)).
  6. Enter the Cash Salary amount (here, $60,000).
  7. Set the Accountable Reimbursement (ARP) — leave at Conference minimum.
  8. Choose the Housing type — Parsonage or Housing Allowance.

Click Calculate.

1 The results table lists every component and the bottom line:

Line itemAmount
Salary$60,000
ARP$3,700
HealthFlex$21,468
Compass$8,910
CPP$2,430
Total Cost to Charge$96,508

The NE total is $96,508. NE's ARP minimum is $3,700, and with ACH billing HealthFlex is the discounted $21,468 rate (it would be $22,596 without ACH).

4.3 — Export a Statement of Understanding (.docx)

Once you have a result, you can save or share it — here, the NE multi-point charge from 4.2.

  1. Copy Table — copies the results table to your clipboard, ready to paste into an email or a Word document (formatting preserved).
  2. Export to SOU (.docx) — downloads a filled-in Statement of Understanding Word document with the figures already in place, ready to review and sign.

Max salary from a budget

Work backwards from a budget: enter what the charge can spend, and the tool finds the largest salary that fits once benefits are covered.

5.1 — Single-point charge

Use case: “Our church has $130,000 budgeted for the pastor. What's the most we can pay in salary after benefits are covered?”
  1. Click Max salary from a budget. The salary box becomes a budget box, and the button changes to Find max salary.
  2. Choose the Clergy / Laity Status (here, Full Elder (FE)).
  3. Enter the Years of Service (here, 13).
  4. Choose the Appointment Time (here, Full-time (100%)).
  5. Enter the Total Budget for the Charge (here, $130,000). Housing, ARP, and all benefits are held as set below, and the tool solves for the salary that fits.

Click Find max salary.

  1. The headline shows the Maximum salary — here, $85,525.47 — the largest salary whose total cost stays within the $130,000 budget.
  2. The same breakdown table shows how that salary plus benefits uses the budget (the total lands right at $130,000).
If a budget is too small to cover even the minimum salary and required benefits, the tool tells you the minimum budget you'd need instead of reporting an impossible salary.

5.2 — Multipoint charge

Use case: “The four churches on the charge have each committed a set dollar amount toward the pastor. What salary does that support?”

In max-salary mode, a multi-point charge shows a linked Share % / Amount table — and, uniquely to this workflow, you can type each church's flat dollar amount in the Amount column (you're not limited to percentages). The two columns stay in sync, and the budget becomes the sum of the amounts.

  1. Choose the Clergy / Laity Status (here, Full Elder (FE)).
  2. Enter the Years of Service (here, 13).
  3. Choose the Appointment Time (here, Full-time (100%)).
  4. The Total Budget fills in automatically — it's the sum of the church amounts you enter below.
  5. Set the Number of Churches (here, 4).
  6. Choose Custom split so each church can carry its own amount.
  7. In the linked table, type each church's dollar amount in the Amount column — Alpha $5,000, Beta $7,000, Gamma $28,000, Delta $90,000. The Share % column derives itself, and the budget becomes $130,000.

Click Find max salary.

1 The Maximum salary is $82,913.37, and each church's column totals its committed amount.

Notice the nuance: the budget is the same $130,000 as the single church in 5.1, but the maximum salary is lower — $82,913.37 vs $85,525.47. A multi-point charge in NY carries the MCAA supplement, so more of the budget goes to fixed benefit costs, leaving a little less for salary.

Tips

  • Abbreviated / Full names toggle (top-left of the results) switches line-item labels between short and full names — handy depending on your audience.
  • Show calculation detail (below the table) explains, in plain language, how each figure was derived and which plan applies and why.
  • Switch conferences (NY / NE) any time — the form stays the same; only the rates and eligibility rules change.
  • Minimum-salary note — if a salary is below the conference minimum for the given status, years, and appointment time, a red note appears so you can double-check.
  • Advanced Settings (bottom of the page, gear icon) holds the editable rate constants for year-to-year updates — most users won't need to touch these.
Figures shown are examples using 2026 rates. Your results will reflect the conference, status, years, appointment, and amounts you enter.
